quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Drop the jaw and pull the tongue back, as if saying 'ah' to a doctor. There is no r sound in RP.
quests.explanation: Long, open and back. In RP the r is silent, so the vowel is all you hear.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɑː/ is back, open and long with unrounded lips; /æ/ is front and shorter, with the tongue pushed forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Wide lips, tongue high, and hold it. The wh is just /w/.
quests.explanation: Held and tense before the dark /l/. A short loose vowel would sound like 'will'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The jaw drops slightly more for /ɪ/ than for /iː/. If your /ɪ/ is turning into /iː/, relax the lips and lower the tongue a little.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Pushed-forward lips and a held vowel, then /t/ shuts it.
quests.explanation: Long and strongly rounded. The loose vowel of 'foot' would be wrong.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are rounded, so the extra cue is tension: /uː/ feels tight, /ʊ/ feels slack.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Half-open jaw, then the /ntʃ/ cluster. The vowel is not as wide as in 'ban'.
quests.explanation: A nasal cluster follows, but the vowel itself is only half open. A wider jaw would drift towards the other vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ and /æ/ differ by about one step of tongue height on the vowel chart: mid-front versus near-open front.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Long, open, back vowel. The r is silent and the mouth stays wide until /k/.
quests.explanation: Ar signals the long open vowel in RP, and the r is silent.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Drop the jaw and pull the tongue back for /ɑː/, as a doctor would ask. For /æ/ the tongue stays forward and the mouth stretches sideways.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Quick and open with slight lip rounding. Then /k/.
quests.explanation: Short, open and rounded. The central vowel would give 'ruck'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In a mirror /ɒ/ shows a round opening and /ʌ/ a relaxed one, with the jaw at about the same height.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Neutral lips, tongue in the middle. 'Mud' is a short grunt.
quests.explanation: Central and unrounded. The wide vowel would give 'mad'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ is among the most open front vowels, while /ʌ/ is only mid-open and central.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: This word surprises many learners: in RP the a is long and open, not like 'glad'.
quests.explanation: A BATH word: the vowel is long and open in RP, and 'grass' and 'class' follow suit.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Front versus back: slide the tongue back with neutral lips for /ɑː/; /æ/ keeps it forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Silent r, a held rounded oval, then /m/.
quests.explanation: Long and rounded. The short vowel belongs in 'stop'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: After the vowel, -or before a consonant (fork, short) usually means /ɔː/, while o before a stop (top, stop) means /ɒ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Both vowels in this pair are short and front. Decide by jaw height: how open is your mouth in 'desk'?
quests.explanation: The jaw is half open. A nearly closed jaw would sound like 'disk'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short front vowels, but /e/ is lower and more open. Let the jaw drop a little further for /e/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Wide lips, long vowel, nothing relaxed about it.
quests.explanation: Held and tense. 'Slip' would use the short loose vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /iː/ is tense and slightly advanced, /ɪ/ more relaxed. You can feel the tension in the muscles under the chin.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Rounded, open and short, unlike the lazy central vowel of 'putt'.
quests.explanation: The lips round slightly. Without rounding it becomes 'putt'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short, so don't wait for a length difference. Wait for darkness (rounding) versus neutrality.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Short and loose with a small mouth gap. 'Sick' is not 'sec'.
quests.explanation: The mouth stays nearly closed. Opening further would give a different word.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Tongue height is the cue: /ɪ/ sits close to high front, /e/ is mid-front with the jaw about half open.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Wide jaw and spread lips, then /mp/ closes the lips.
quests.explanation: Low and front, and the vowel before /mp/ stays wide.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling won't tell you: a gives /e/ in 'many' and /æ/ in 'cat', and ea gives /e/ in 'head'. Decide with ears and jaw.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Lips pushed forward, vowel held. Compare it with 'full': this one has tension.
quests.explanation: Rounded lips held for the whole vowel. With loose lips you would say 'full'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Don't over-lengthen /ʊ/: a held, pouting vowel in 'book' sounds foreign.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Open the jaw and keep the vowel long. Silent r again.
quests.explanation: Ar plus a consonant gives the long open vowel in RP.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In RP many words with a before f, s, th or n plus a consonant take /ɑː/ (the BATH set). That is a vocabulary fact, not a spelling rule.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Mid-open jaw, tongue mid-front, then the /kst/ cluster closes it.
quests.explanation: The jaw is half open. The other vowel would need a nearly closed mouth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Duration is similar, so rely on openness: a small mouth gap for /ɪ/, a slightly larger one for /e/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: A wide mouth after the /kr/ cluster, with the tongue forward.
quests.explanation: 'Crush' would use a central neutral vowel and is a different word.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Common u words (cut, bus) and some o words (love, come) take /ʌ/. The spelling o misleads here.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Silent r, oval lips, one held vowel. Where does the jaw sit compared with 'fox'?
quests.explanation: Long and rounded. The short vowel belongs in 'fox'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Don't add an r in RP, but remember the vowel carries the whole syllable, so hold /ɔː/ fully.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Short and loose, followed by a dark /l/. Your lips should not spread.
quests.explanation: Short and lax. Tensing and spreading the lips would give 'beel', which is not a word.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both vowels are high and front, so the gap is small. Listen for a slight brightness in /iː/ rather than a huge difference.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: In RP, a before n plus a consonant is often long and open. Say it as 'dahnss'.
quests.explanation: A BATH word: long and open in RP, as in 'chance' and 'France'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: If you can hold the vowel indefinitely with an open mouth, it is /ɑː/. /æ/ is quick and bright.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Rounded and open. 'Shock' has a clear lip oval.
quests.explanation: The lips are rounded. Unrounded, it would become 'shuck'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: If /ʌ/ keeps coming out as /ɒ/, relax the lips completely and let the tongue rest in the middle.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Short and loose, with a jaw that stays nearly closed.
quests.explanation: Opening the jaw would shift it to the half-open vowel and distort the word.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Keep the lips relaxed for /ɪ/, not stretched as for /iː/. /e/ is only a half-open smile.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Short, lax, loose lips; the /ʃ/ ends it quickly.
quests.explanation: The same short vowel as in 'push' and 'put'. Pushing the lips forward would give 'boosh'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʊ/ is lax with loosely rounded lips and a tongue pulled slightly forward; /uː/ is tense, high and back with tightly rounded, protruded lips.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Open the jaw wide and let it fall, then /d/. It isn't 'said'.
quests.explanation: A wide mouth. A half-open one would sound like 'said'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The contrast is clearest in stressed syllables; in weak syllables both tend to drift towards a neutral vowel.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The au spelling gives a long rounded vowel; then /ntʃ/.
quests.explanation: Au is a dependable spelling for the long rounded vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Words spelled aw or au (saw, sauce) take /ɔː/ reliably, while a after w can go either way.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The eart spelling is a trap: say it like 'hart'.
quests.explanation: Ea spells the long open vowel here, but a different vowel in 'earth' and another in 'hear'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: BATH words (class, path, plant, dance, half) are one of the biggest differences between RP and other accents. Follow the RP set.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Jaw about half open: 'mess' is not 'miss'.
quests.explanation: Closing the jaw would turn it into 'miss', so keep it half open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short front vowels, but /e/ is lower and more open. Let the jaw drop a little further for /e/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Lips neutral, tongue central. It isn't 'dram'.
quests.explanation: Relaxed and central. A wide, forward vowel would give 'dram'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In a mirror /æ/ shows a visibly wide mouth, /ʌ/ a smaller one with lax lips.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: After /kw/ the vowel is held with spread lips.
quests.explanation: Spread lips, tense tongue and held length, even after the rounded /kw/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Check the corners of the mouth: they pull back for /iː/ but stay roughly neutral for /ɪ/.
